rules: CS_RANK($close - TS_MAX($high, 21)) and CS_RANK($close / (TS_MAX($high, 21) + 1e-8)) mix adjusted $close with raw $high, yet both were accepted this round with the 2nd and 3rd highest fitness (4.553, 4.780). Given the known adjusted-vs-raw scale mismatch, audit whether that mixing inflated their scores before trusting them further, and flag any new $close-vs-$open/$high/$low expression the same way.

TS_DELTA of a fundamental (roe, leverage, asset_turnover, operating_margin, earnings_per_share) at 21-63 day windows failed the cheap screen three times (|t| 0.07-0.53). TS_DELTA($leverage, 126) paired with a level term (CS_RANK($roe)) passed at fitness 3.859: prefer 126+ day windows for fundamental deltas, and pair a delta with a level rather than two deltas together.

$accrual_gap (coverage 0.872) and the 126-day delta of $operating_margin (coverage 0.882) both missed the 0.90 bar by a similar margin, pointing to sparse reporting for these fields in this universe. Deprioritize them until coverage improves at the data layer.

5 of 20 rejections were archive_subtree near-duplicates, and each was only a window tweak (21 to 42, 2 to 5) or an added multiplier on an already-archived tree, never a structural change. The earnings_per_share/close ratio subtree alone accounted for 2 of them; change the operator or feature, not just the window, near these trees.

A mechanically similar feature or operator swap without structural change reads as a duplicate, not a diversification: $volume in place of $dollar_volume scored rho 0.850 against an existing member, and EMA in place of TS_MEAN at the same window scored rho 0.996. Pair any such substitution with a genuine structural change.

Both crossover_not_a_fusion rejections used CS_RANK($roa), a 2-node wrapped-leaf archive member, as a parent; that size can never meet the fusion donation requirement. Exclude bare single-feature CS_RANK(feature) members from the fusion parent pool.

3 of 20 rejections were exact within-run duplicates: CS_RANK($roa) plus two high-low-range/dollar-volume normalization variants. De-duplicate the candidate pool before scoring, especially around that feature family.

The round's top 3 fitness scores (5.128, 4.780, 4.553) all paired a fundamental level or a close-vs-high price-distance term with a volume-liquidity normalizer (CS_ZSCORE or TS_RANK of $dollar_volume). This pairing is outperforming pure return/fundamental combos; prioritize it next round.
